question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related to qualifications for appointment as Governor?
solution:
The correct answer is **__157.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Article 157__ **of the **__Indian Constitution__ **is related to __**qualifications **__for **__appointment __**as **__Governor__****.**

 __
 
• It is necessary to study **Articles 155 **and** 157 together.**
 
• According to **Article 155, **the **Governor** must be **chosen **by the **President**, hence the **Union Government **is allowed to choose anybody it sees fit to lead any** State as Governor.**
 
• The **Governor **may be seen as the **representation **of the whole in the part because the Union is the whole and **each State **is a **component** **portion **of it.
 
• It should be **emphasised **that despite what its minor header claims,** Article 157 **does not really specify any **requirements **for appointment as governor, other than the requirements that the applicant be an **Indian citizen **and reach the **age of 35. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The sort and calibre of people who were appointed as governors received** no criticism** for nearly **20 years **following the **Constitution's inception.**
 
• However, for a number of years now, there has been much **criticism **of the **individuals nominated**.
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission **recommended and the **Constitution Commission **agreed that when choosing a **governor**, consideration should be given to the following factors: 
 
 
• He should be **eminent **in **some field; **
 
• He should come from **outside **the **State**;
 
• He should be a **detached figure **and not too closely associated with the **local politics **of the State;
 
• He should be a person who has not **participated **too **significantly **in **politics **generally, and especially in the racial arena.
